messages:
Security Ops: @here Security advisory: starting a 14-day enforcement window for long-lived service credentials. Any svc token or static API key with TTL > 24h will be subject to automated revocation after the window. Please read and act. :warning:

Maria Chen: Quick clarification — does this include tokens stored in Vault with rotation enabled?

Security Ops: If Vault rotates them automatically and the effective TTL < 24h, you're OK. The enforcement targets tokens issued without short-lived rotation or listed in the token inventory as >24h.

Aj Patel: We have legacy deploy keys in some CI jobs that can't use OIDC yet. Migration plan?

Security Ops: Prefer OIDC-based flows where possible. For GitHub Actions, use aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials or equivalent. If not possible, open an exception ticket to #eng-sre with tag "ephemeral-exception" and include compensating controls (IP allowlist, HSM, rigorous logging).

Lina Gomez: Is there a way to find all affected services quickly?

Security Ops: Yes — owners with inventory access can run the inventory query. We'll also publish a CSV of impacted services at https://internal.redwood/policies/pc-2026-04.

SRE oncall: Timeline: dry-run audit next Tuesday (no revocations), enforced revocation after the 14-day grace. We'll post exact times.

Aj Patel: Copy. I'll roll our CI to OIDC this week and update the ticket when done.

Security Ops: Action checklist: 1) Audit token inventory, 2) Migrate tokens to <24h TTL or OIDC, 3) Rotate static keys now, 4) Open exception ticket if you cannot migrate. We'll host a short Q&A and a migration checklist doc later today.

deploy-bot: policy-change created: service-credentials-ttl-enforcement (id: pc-2026-04).

Maria Chen: Thanks, starting rotation now. :thumbsup:

Lina Gomez: Opening exception ticket for batch pipeline (can't use OIDC without infra changes).

SRE oncall: We'll review exceptions within 48 hours. Ping me for pairing.

Security Ops: Thanks everyone — reach out if you hit blockers.
